label: accepted

evidence.V1: Faceted mossy slab with a companion pebble reads as a rock from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette (angular polygon outline); clear at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big slab, medium pebble and moss cap, small chamfer bands and facet planes: clear hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised low rock: broad tilted top plane, chunky facets, small pebble for scale contrast.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistent soft chamfers that catch a light band along the top edge in the facets close-up; moss cap edge also chamfered.
evidence.V5: Facets shade cleanly, but the pebble close-up shows a star-shaped specular pinch where several facets converge on one vertex (also visible as a bright point in the three-quarter view); minor.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in three values plus one moss green secondary; disciplined, strong contrast; sandstone/basalt colourways keep the scheme.
evidence.V7: 188 tris vs rock target 400 (ceiling 1000): well under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, designed facets with chamfers, stone + moss palette as the nature kit specifies: matches.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

evidence.V1: Tilted moss-topped wedge plus side pebble reads as a rock in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view still reads, though the foreshortened pebble looks like a thin stalk.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big wedge mass, medium moss cap and facets, small pebble at the foot.
evidence.V3: Main wedge with a sloped moss top has some character, but the pebble is an awkward tall shard that in top view reads like a stick, weakening the stylised read.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with soft chamfers; the cream-lit band under the moss catches a consistent rounded highlight along its edges.
evidence.V5: Pebble close-up (studio) shows a star-shaped specular pinch where several facets converge at one vertex, and soft smearing across facets on the pebble; main rock otherwise clean.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in 3 values plus one moss green; redrock/slate colourways keep the same discipline.
evidence.V7: 188 tris vs rock target 400 - under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, designed facets, stone + moss secondary as in the Nature spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Reads as a mossy rock with a companion pebble in front, 3/4, top and silhouette; outline is a chunky polygon with the pebble as a secondary lump.
evidence.V2: Big slab + small pebble + moss cap give two clear tiers, but the medium tier is weak: the main mass is only ~6 large facets with no secondary chips or ledges.
evidence.V3: Low wedge slab (3.0 x 2.4 x 1.0 studs) with a planar moss top reads somewhat like a sliced block; the pebble is a confident chunk, the main rock is a bit stiff.
evidence.V4: Facet borders are softened by smooth shading rather than crisp chamfers: some edges read crisp (front lower edge), others smear into gradients (moss rim band, right-hand corner) - inconsistent.
evidence.V5: No seams or z-fighting, but weighted-normal smoothing over large facets leaves smeared highlight streaks (3/4 view below the moss band) and a star-shaped point highlight where pebble facets converge (pebble close-up).
evidence.V6: One stone grey in ~3 values plus one moss green; colourways (basalt+teal, sandstone) stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material and nature palette fit, but rocks should read as designed flat facets; here facets are blurred by smooth shading, so the edge language differs slightly from the kit.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Star-shaped shading pinch at the pebble's converging vertex
Specular pinch / star highlight at the pebble's apex vertex where facets converge (Rock_01_close_pebble_studio.png)
Soft smeared shading across pebble facets instead of crisp flat facets
Smeared highlight streak across facets below the moss rim (3/4 and basalt colourway)
Star-shaped converging highlight on the pebble's top vertex
top_fixes: Split/chamfer the pebble's pole vertex or set its facets flat so the converging-vertex pinch disappears
Let the moss cap drape slightly over one edge (uneven boundary) instead of a flat lid
Optionally add one crack or step facet on the long front face for an extra small-scale read
Split normals / add weighted normals on the pebble so its facets shade flat and the apex pinch disappears
Reshape the pebble to a squatter chunk so it does not read as a stalk from above
Optionally add a second tiny pebble to balance the composition
Split normals / add small chamfers on facet borders so facets read flat and crisp instead of smeared
Break up the main mass with 2-3 medium chips or a ledge so there is a medium tier
Give the moss a slightly irregular edge/drape over the rim instead of a perfectly planar top cap
Tilt or round the top so the rock reads less like a sliced wedge
